title: Fabrication of SnO 2 /rGO nanocatalyst for the multicomponent synthesis of imidazole derivatives
content: A tin oxide/reduced graphene oxide (SnO2/rGO) nanocatalyst was prepared and evaluated as a heterogeneous Lewis acid catalyst for the one-pot, three-component synthesis of 2,4,5-trisubstituted imidazole derivatives. Characterization by XRD, FTIR spectroscopy, Raman spectroscopy, FESEM-EDS, TEM-SAED, and XPS supported the formation of crystalline SnO2 nanoparticles dispersed on wrinkled rGO sheets. TEM showed particle diameters of approximately 7–15 nm, whereas ICP-OES confirms 4.81 wt% Sn present within the bulk sample. Under the optimized conditions (25 mg catalyst, ethanol, 80 °C, and 1 h), the reaction afforded isolated yields of 88–98% for the aldehydes examined. SnO2/rGO gave a higher yield than SnO2, GO, or rGO under identical screening conditions, consistent with improved dispersion and accessibility of Lewis-acidic Sn4+ sites on the rGO support. The catalyst retained activity over five cycles, with the isolated yield decreasing from 97% to 91%, and the recovered material retained the principal XRD reflections of tetragonal rutile SnO2. No Sn was detected in the reaction filtrate by ICP-AES within the analytical detection limit. The calculated reaction-level metrics included an atom economy of 66%, a minimum E-factor of 0.54, and a maximum carbon efficiency of 90%; these values exclude solvents, purification, washing, catalyst preparation, water, and energy. These results identify SnO2/rGO as a reusable heterogeneous catalyst for this multicomponent transformation.
